questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A,$ $Σ,$ and $V$ shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ what is the second column of $U?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ and ${\sigma }_{i}\ne 0,$ then the $i$th column of $U$ can be found as

$$
{u}_{i}=\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{i}}A{v}_{i},
$$

 

where ${v}_{i}$ is the $i$th column of the matrix $V.$

From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that the singular values are ${\sigma }_{1}=9$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=1.$ Therefore, the second column of $U$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{2} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{2}}A{v}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 4 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}{v}_{11} & {v}_{12} \\ {v}_{21} & {v}_{22}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ what is the value of $|{v}_{11}|+|{v}_{21}|?$
questions.worked_solution:
If $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ the columns of $V$ must be the right singular vectors of $A,$ i.e., the unit eigenvectors of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that the singular values are ${\sigma }_{1}=7$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=3.$ So, the first column of $V$ corresponds to the singular value ${\sigma }_{1}=7.$

Hence, we need to find a unit eigenvector of ${A}^{T}\,A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}={\sigma }_{1}^{2}=49.$ 

- Computing ${A}^{T}\,A,$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}-5 & 4 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}-5 & 4 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 4 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-5 & 4 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}41 & -16 \\ -16 & 17\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- Computing ${A}^{T}\,A-49I,$ we get

$$
{A}^{T}\,A-49I=[\begin{aligned}41 & -16 \\ -16 & 17\end{aligned}]-49[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-8 & -16 \\ -16 & -32\end{aligned}]
$$

- Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-49I)v=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Dividing $v$ by its norm, we get 

$$
\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
|{v}_{11}|+|{v}_{21}|=|-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}|+|\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}|=\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}8 & -3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $Σ$ shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the matrices $U$ and $V?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's find the singular value decomposition of $A$ using the usual algorithm.

- **Step 1.** Compute ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}8 & -3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}8 & -3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 3 \\ -3 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}8 & -3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}73 & -24 \\ -24 & 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step 2.** Find the singular values: From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that ${\sigma }_{1}=9$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=1.$

- **Step 3.** Find the right singular vectors of $A$ (i.e., the unit eigenvectors of ${A}^{T}\,A$):

- For ${\lambda }_{1}={\sigma }_{1}^{2}=81,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-81I & =[\begin{aligned}73 & -24 \\ -24 & 9\end{aligned}]-81[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-8 & -24 \\ -24 & -72\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-81I)v=0$ gives a unit eigenvector

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}={\sigma }_{2}^{2}=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-I & =[\begin{aligned}73 & -24 \\ -24 & 9\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}72 & -24 \\ -24 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-I)v=0$ gives a unit eigenvector

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}].
$$

- **Step 4.** Find the left singular vectors of $A$: Since we know the singular values and right singular vectors, we can compute the columns of $U$ as follows:

- First, we compute ${u}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{1}}A{v}_{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}8 & -3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}-\frac{27}{\sqrt{10}} \\ -\frac{9}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- Then, we compute ${u}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{2} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{2}}A{v}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}8 & -3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we construct the matrices $U$ and $V:$

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]
$$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $Σ$ shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the matrices $U$ and $V?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's find the singular value decomposition of $A$ using the usual algorithm.

- **Step 1.** Compute ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 2 & 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step 2.** Find the singular values: From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that ${\sigma }_{1}=3$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=2.$

- **Step 3.** Find the right singular vectors of $A$ (i.e., the unit eigenvectors of ${A}^{T}\,A$):

- For ${\lambda }_{1}={\sigma }_{1}^{2}=9,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-9I & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 2 & 8\end{aligned}]-9[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-9I)v=0$ gives a unit eigenvector

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}={\sigma }_{2}^{2}=4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-4I & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 2 & 8\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-4I)v=0$ gives a unit eigenvector

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}].
$$

- **Step 4.** Find the left singular vectors of $A.$: Since we know the singular values and right singular vectors, we can compute the columns of $U$ as follows:

- First, we compute ${u}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{1}}A{v}_{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- Then, we compute ${u}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{2} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{2}}A{v}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we construct the matrices $U$ and $V:$

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]
$$
